section: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 and amendments; Civil Rights Protection Act 1955
subsections: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:
1. Section 3 deals with atrocities committed by persons who are not members of a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe.
2. The Act creates certain offences which are not covered by the Protection of Civil Rights Act or the Indian Penal Code.
3. The Act applies only when the accused and the victim belong to the same Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Act principally covers offences by non-SC/ST persons against SC/ST persons.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the scope of the accused and victim rather than accepting a broad statement about applicability.

accepted.s: Wilful neglect of duty by a public servant under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is dealt with under:
o: Section 3
Section 14
Section 19
Section 4
accepted.x: Section 4 provides punishment for wilful neglect of duty by a public servant.
accepted.tq: Match the official duty-related offence with its precise statutory section.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the special judicial structure under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: Special Courts are established only by the Supreme Court without consultation with the State judiciary.
Special Courts are established in every district with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court.
Exclusive Special Courts existed in the original 1989 Act and were not affected by later amendments.
Trials under the Act can be conducted only by ordinary Magistrates.
accepted.x: Special Courts are set up in each district with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court. Exclusive Special Courts were added by the 2015 amendment.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who establishes or concurs’ method to avoid confusing the State Government, High Court and Supreme Court.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Section 19 of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is correct?
o: It provides for probation in all cases involving first-time offenders.
It bars probation for persons convicted under the Act.
It provides for an appeal to the High Court within 90 days.
It deals with the definition of economic boycott.
accepted.x: Section 19 provides that the benefit of probation is not available to persons convicted under the Act.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the sentencing restriction in Section 19 from appeal and definition provisions in nearby sections.

accepted.s: The rule-making power under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is vested in:
o: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes
The Supreme Court of India
The Central Government
The State Government alone
accepted.x: Section 23 vests the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act in the Central Government.
accepted.tq: Ask ‘who would make rules?’ and distinguish the rule-making authority from implementing authorities.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the scope and operation of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989:
1. It applies to offences committed by non-SC/ST persons against members of SCs or STs.
2. The offences under the Act are cognizable.
3. Arrest without warrant is permissible for such offences.
4. The Act has applied to Jammu and Kashmir since 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Act covers specified offences by non-SC/ST persons against SC/ST persons, treats them as cognizable, permits arrest without warrant, and has applied to Jammu and Kashmir since 2019.
accepted.tq: Check scope, procedural character and territorial application separately before choosing the coded combination.

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a provision associated with the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989?
o: Grant of arms licences to members of SCs and STs
Enhanced punishment for public servants in specified circumstances
Cancellation of arms licences in atrocity-prone areas
Automatic dissolution of every local authority located in an atrocity-prone area
accepted.x: The Act provides for cancellation of arms licences of potential offenders in atrocity-prone areas, licences for SC/ST persons and enhanced punishment for public servants. It does not provide for automatic dissolution of local authorities.
accepted.tq: Find the option that introduces an institutional consequence not connected with the Act’s stated safeguards.

accepted.s: An offence under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act committed on or after 1 July 2024 is to be read with references to the:
o: CPC and Evidence Act respectively
IPC and CrPC only
BNS and BNSS respectively
PCRA and BNSS respectively
accepted.x: Since 1 July 2024, references to the IPC and CrPC in the Act are read as references to the corresponding provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.
accepted.tq: Use the one-to-one replacement pair: IPC becomes BNS and CrPC becomes BNSS.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct combination regarding investigation under the Protection of Civil Rights and Atrocities Rules, 1995?
o: Investigation by an officer not below DSP rank; charge-sheet within 60 days
Investigation by an officer not below Inspector rank; charge-sheet within 30 days
Investigation by an officer not below Superintendent of Police rank; charge-sheet within 90 days
Investigation by an Executive Magistrate; charge-sheet within 60 days
accepted.x: Investigation is to be conducted by a police officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police, and the investigation and filing of the charge-sheet are to be completed within 60 days.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair of investigating rank and then verify the prescribed time limit.
accepted.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

accepted.s: Under the PoA Rules, 1995, the annual report on implementation of the Act is prepared by:
o: The Central Government on the basis of reports received from the States and submitted to Parliament
The concerned State Government and submitted to the district administration
The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes and submitted to the Supreme Court
The Special Public Prosecutor and submitted to the High Court
accepted.x: The Centre prepares the annual report on implementation using reports received from the States and places it before Parliament.
accepted.tq: Trace the reporting chain from State reports to the Central Government and finally Parliament.
accepted.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

accepted.s: The monetary relief and rehabilitation provided under the PoA Rules, 1995 ranges from:
o: ₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh
₹1 lakh to ₹10 lakh
accepted.x: The relief and rehabilitation amount, fixed in 2016, ranges from ₹85,000 to ₹8.25 lakh.
accepted.tq: Retain both endpoints of the range and avoid replacing the lower or upper figure with a rounded amount.
accepted.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

accepted.s: The relief paid to victims under the centrally sponsored scheme for implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights and Atrocities provisions is shared between the Centre and the States in the ratio of:
accepted.x: The relief is paid under a centrally sponsored scheme on a 50:50 Centre-State basis.
accepted.tq: Use the exact Centre-State sharing ratio rather than confusing it with ratios used in other schemes.
accepted.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding monitoring under the PoA Rules, 1995:
1. Monitoring takes place at the district level.
2. Monitoring takes place at the State level.
3. Monitoring takes place at the national level.
4. The Rules provide only for judicial monitoring and not administrative monitoring.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Monitoring is undertaken at district, State and national levels. Statement 4 is false because the framework is not limited to judicial monitoring.
accepted.tq: Identify the complete three-level structure and reject the restrictive ‘only’ statement.
accepted.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

accepted.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Rules were notified in:
accepted.x: The Protection of Civil Rights Rules were notified in 1977.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the Rules from the years of the parent Acts and the PoA Rules.
accepted.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

accepted.s: At the Central level, implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Rules involves the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Which of the following ministries is NOT identified with that implementation?
o: Ministry of Minority Affairs
The ministries identified for implementation at the Centre
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Home Affairs
accepted.x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs is not the ministry identified for implementation in the stated Central-level arrangement.
accepted.tq: Use the ministry-swapping trap and identify the neighbouring but incorrect department.
accepted.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

accepted.s: The Centre’s scheme for implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights and Atrocities provisions proposed relief for approximately how many atrocity victims?
accepted.x: The scheme proposed relief for approximately 87,426 atrocity victims.
accepted.tq: Test the exact estimate by distinguishing the nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief

accepted.s: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Amendment Act, 2015 came into force in:
accepted.x: The 2015 Amendment Act was enforced from 2016.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of the amendment from the year in which it was brought into force.

accepted.s: Which of the following was introduced or specifically recognised as a new atrocity by the 2015 amendment to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act?
o: Failure to pay a civil debt
Garlanding a person with footwear
Refusal to provide a commercial loan to any person
Disagreement with a local authority’s tax assessment
accepted.x: Garlanding an SC/ST person with footwear was included among the new or rephrased atrocities under the 2015 amendment.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise act included in the amended offence list rather than a general civil dispute.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with a new atrocity recognised under the 2015 amendment?
o: Forcing a person to carry or dispose of a carcass — new atrocity
Dedicating an SC/ST woman as a devadasi — new atrocity
Issuing a general public notice for a government recruitment examination — new atrocity
Tonsuring — new atrocity
accepted.x: Tonsuring, forcing a person to carry or dispose of a carcass and dedicating an SC/ST woman as a devadasi are recognised acts under the amended framework. Issuing a general recruitment notice is not such an atrocity.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated administrative act among a cluster of specific amended offences.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding offences added or rephrased by the 2015 amendment:
1. Denying access to irrigation facilities may constitute an atrocity.
2. Forcing a person to perform manual scavenging may constitute an atrocity.
3. Preventing SC/ST candidates from contesting an election may constitute an atrocity.
4. Calling a woman a witch is included among the specified atrocities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements describe acts included among the new or rephrased atrocities under the 2015 amendment.
accepted.tq: Use complete-list recognition: verify each concrete act before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: The 2015 amendment specifically recognised which of the following as an atrocity?
o: A civil disagreement over inheritance between persons of the same community
Refusal by a voter to support a particular candidate
Failure of a private employer to grant promotion on seniority
Social or economic boycott of an SC/ST person
accepted.x: Social or economic boycott was added as an atrocity, and “economic boycott” was separately defined in the amended Act.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a legally defined boycott from ordinary private disputes or political disagreement.

accepted.s: Under the 2015 amendment, the trial in an Exclusive Special Court is intended to be completed within:
o: 120 days of commencement of investigation
60 days of filing of the charge-sheet
90 days of arrest of the accused
30 days of registration of the FIR
accepted.x: The amendment envisages completion of trial within two months, that is, 60 days, from the filing of the charge-sheet.
accepted.tq: Convert the stated period of two months into the precise numerical option and note the starting point.

accepted.s: Which of the following was a major institutional change introduced by the 2015 amendment?
o: Abolition of Special Public Prosecutors
Transfer of all trials to ordinary civil courts
Creation of Exclusive Special Courts and Exclusive Special Public Prosecutors
Removal of the power of Special Courts to take direct cognizance
accepted.x: The amendment added Exclusive Special Courts and Exclusive Special Public Prosecutors. It also permitted Special Courts to take direct cognizance.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed institutional changes and identify the paired additions made by the amendment.

accepted.s: The 2015 amendment introduced a new chapter dealing with:
o: Regulation of civil marriages
Taxation of charitable institutions
Appointment of village revenue officers
Rights of victims and witnesses
accepted.x: A new chapter on the rights of victims and witnesses was introduced by the 2015 amendment.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment with its distinctive new chapter rather than with unrelated social legislation.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly reflects the power of Special Courts after the 2015 amendment?
o: They have no power to take cognizance and can only record evidence.
They may take cognizance only after prior approval of the Central Government.
They may take direct cognizance of offences under the Act.
They may take cognizance only after a civil court’s decree.
accepted.x: The 2015 amendment enabled Special Courts to take direct cognizance of offences under the Act.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority can act directly and reject added approval requirements not found in the provision.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Enactment of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
B. Commencement of the Act
C. Enactment of the 2015 Amendment Act
D. Insertion of Section 18A
E. Extension of the Act to Jammu and Kashmir
o: A, B, C, D, E
B, A, C, E, D
A, C, B, D, E
A, B, D, C, E
accepted.x: The Act was enacted in 1989, commenced in 1990, amended in 2015, Section 18A was inserted in 2018, and its application extended to Jammu and Kashmir in 2019.
accepted.tq: Fix the first two dates, then place the 2015 amendment, 2018 insertion and 2019 territorial extension.

accepted.s: A police officer receives a complaint involving an offence under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. Which course is consistent with the statutory framework?
o: The investigation may be conducted by any constable and the charge-sheet may be filed whenever convenient.
The matter must be transferred to a civil court for preliminary adjudication.
The investigation should be conducted by an officer not below DSP rank and completed with charge-sheet filing within 60 days.
The case must first undergo a preliminary enquiry and receive approval before arrest in every instance.
accepted.x: The PoA Rules require investigation by an officer not below the rank of DSP and completion with charge-sheet filing in the Special Court within 60 days. Section 18A removes the requirement of preliminary enquiry or approval before arrest.
accepted.tq: Combine the rank, time-limit and arrest-procedure rules in a practical fact pattern.
accepted.sec: PoA Rules 1995 - investigation, annual report, relief
